articles.title: 76ers rule out LeBron James, Joel Embiid vs. Hornets
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers have ruled out LeBron James and Joel Embiid for Saturday night’s road matchup against the Charlotte Hornets as the organization manage...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers have ruled out LeBron James and Joel Embiid for Saturday night's road matchup against the Charlotte Hornets as the organization manages both stars' injuries during the second half of a back-to-back.

Philadelphia's latest injury report lists James as out due to low back/sciatica management, while Embiid will sit because of right foot plantar fascia injury management.

The 76ers (5-1) enter Saturday's contest following a 98-93 victory over the New York Knicks in Friday night's NBA Cup opener, extending their strong start to the 2026-27 season.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

James and Embiid both played significant minutes in the victory despite Philadelphia missing Jaylen Brown, who was ruled out shortly before tip-off with left patellar tendinopathy.

James finished with 20 points, nine rebounds, eight assists, one steal and one block across 34 minutes. The 41-year-old shot 8-for-15 from the field and 2-for-6 from beyond the arc.

Embiid contributed 10 points, seven rebounds, seven assists, one steal and one block in 33 minutes. The 32-year-old struggled offensively, shooting 3-for-12 from the field and missing all four of his 3-point attempts.

76ers face additional injury concerns against Hornets

Through five appearances, James is averaging 16.4 points, seven rebounds, seven assists, 1.6 steals and one block while shooting 44.9% from the field.

Embiid is averaging 19.2 points, 9.4 rebounds, 5.2 assists and one block across 35.2 minutes per game, shooting 40% from the field.

Philadelphia's injury report also lists Dominick Barlow (low back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon rupture) as out.

Brown remains questionable with left patellar tendinopathy, alongside Tacko Fall (left quadriceps strain) and Jabari Walker (left patellar tendinopathy).

With James and Embiid unavailable, Philadelphia could rely more heavily on Tyrese Maxey and its remaining rotation players to maintain its early-season momentum.

The 76ers will face the Hornets (3-3) Saturday at 6 p.m. ET on NBA TV.

articles.title: Analyst urges Houston to consider Kyrie Irving trade
articles.summary: After the Houston Rockets’ loss to the Dallas Mavericks in NBA Cup group play on Friday, one analyst believes the Rockets should go all in on trading for Kyr...
articles.body:
After the Houston Rockets ' loss to the Dallas Mavericks in NBA Cup group play on Friday, one analyst believes the Rockets should go all in on trading for Kyrie Irving . The Dallas Mavericks pulled off a clutch-time victory over the Rockets, winning 116-111. Irving finished with 35 points, 9 assists, and 4 rebounds, and knocked down 5 three-pointers.

Following the game on Saturday afternoon, SiriusXM NBA Radio analyst Sam Mitchell said he believes the Rockets should push the trade for Irving. Mitchell started by saying Irving has exceeded expectations in Dallas, especially given the doubts about how he would look after his injury.

"Kyrie is making everybody on that team better. Everybody thought this was going to be a down year for Dallas with a young coach straight from college, with all these young players transitioning to building this team around Cooper. Nobody knew what Kyrie was going to look like. Man, Kyrie looked better than he did before he got hurt."

He then addressed Irving's trade value , arguing a team could land him without giving up a huge haul.

"You might be able to get two first-round picks for Kyrie [unclear: "down"], and that's a lot for a 34-year-old injured point guard who missed all of last year with an injury."

Mitchell then named the Rockets as the team that should make the move, saying Houston's competition in the West makes the timing ideal.

"I'll tell you right now: the Houston Rockets. You put him on the Houston Rockets, you put him on the Houston Rockets with the injuries in the rest of the West, it might be over. They are clearly the best team with Kyrie out there."

If the Rockets were to trade for Irving, it would be a reunion for Kevin Durant, who played with Irving in Brooklyn before the championship-winning point guard was sent to the Dallas Mavericks. Durant was traded to the Phoenix Suns at the 2023 trade deadline.

articles.title: Rangers' Joc Pederson, Kyle Higashioka and Jakob Junis decline mutual options
articles.summary: ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Designated hitter Joc Pederson, catcher Kyle Higashioka and right-hander Jakob Junis declined their mutual options with the Texas Ran...
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Designated hitter Joc Pederson, catcher Kyle Higashioka and right-hander Jakob Junis declined their mutual options with the Texas Rangers, the team said Saturday.

All three became eligible for free agency.

Pederson turned down an $18 million option that did not include a buyout, part of a $37 million, two-year contract . The 34-year-old, a two-time All-Star, hit .235 with 26 homers and 53 RBIs in 136 games. He did not play after Sept. 12, when he fractured his left wrist upon getting hit by a 93.3 mph fastball from Arizona's Brandon Pfaadt.

Higashioka declined a $7 million option and gets a $1 million buyout, completing a $13.5 million, two-year contract . The 36-year-old hit .218 with seven homers and 18 RBIs in 56 games this year. He played his last major league game on July 20 because of a right flexor strain , then played in 11 games at Triple-A Round Rock from Sept. 4-20 during an injury rehabilitation assignment.

Junis turned down a $5 million option and receives a $1.25 million buyout as part of a $4 million, one-year contract . The 34-year-old was 1-3 with a 3.64 ERA in 52 relief appearances. He didn't pitch between June 29 and July 18 because of hip impingement and between July 28 and Aug. 15 because of a left adductor strain.

articles.title: Recital del Casademont Zaragoza para reventar al FIATC Girona
articles.standfirst: Vives (21+3+7), Birutis (15+8), Jaworski 817+1+4) y Bell-Haynes (13+2+9) lideran el triunfo maño
articles.summary: Vives (21+3+7), Birutis (15+8), Jaworski 817+1+4) y Bell-Haynes (13+2+9) lideran el triunfo maño
articles.body: El Casademont Zaragoza pasó página este sábado de la dolorosa derrota contra el Barça con una sólida victoria contra el FIATC Girona (107-78) en el Pabellón Príncipe Felipe para afianzarse entre los ocho primeros clasificados. El equipo de Gonzalo García consiguió el cuarto triunfo en seis jornadas, con una gran segunda parte (59-38) y cuatro hombres por encima de los 20 créditos de valoración: Guillem Vives (21 puntos y siete asistencias), Justin Jaworski (17), Laurynas Birutis (15 puntos y ocho rebotes) y el recuperado Trae Bell-Haynes (13). El cuadro de Moncho Fernández buscaba demostrar que el tropiezo europeo en la pista del NHSZ-Szolnoki Olajbanyasz húngaro solo fue una anécdota, pero se vio superado en Zaragoza y encajó la tercera derrota contundente en tres desplazamientos en la Liga Endesa, después de caer por 118-78 contra el Kosner Baskonia y por 115-92 contra el Río Breogán. La buena actuación de Jassel Pérez (19), líder de la ACB en puntos y segundo en valoración, no fue suficiente, en un partido que se decidió por las diferencias en el triple: 13/25 (52%) por 7/30 (23%). El partido empezó con mucha igualdad (8-7) entre dos conjuntos que querían reencontrarse con la victoria y que llegaban empatados en la clasificación de la ACB con un balance de 3/2. Se sucedían las alternativas entre los dos equipos y las acciones de mérito de Jaworski, autor de ocho de los primeros 18 puntos (18-14), y de Jassel Pérez. El Girona cerró el primer cuarto dos puntos por debajo (23-21) por su desacierto en los triples (2/9) y volvía a demostrar su debilidad en los tiros libres, un problema crónico en este inicio de temporada. Jaworski aumentó la máxima ventaja aragonesa hasta los seis puntos con un 3+1 para inaugurar el segundo período (27-21) y prosiguió el intercambio de golpes entre ambos conjuntos. Los visitantes seguían erráticos desde más allá de la línea de 6,75 metros (2/14), pero seguían dentro del partido gracias a su poderío en la pintura (31-28). Jaworski alcanzó los 15 puntos con su tercer triple en tres intentos (36-30) y la renta local llegó a nueve puntos tras tres triples de Robert Blumbergs, Guillem Vives y Bell-Haynes (46-37). El Zaragoza, de menos a más, lucía un 54% de acierto en triples (7/13) por el 19% visitante y al descanso vencía por 48-40 (25-19). Los locales fueron alimentando su ventaja en el inicio de la segunda mitad y se escaparon a 16 puntos tras sendos triples de Bell-Haynes y Miguel González (62-46), a 18 tras ocho puntos consecutivos de Vives (74-57) y a 19 tras otro triple de Nico Brussino (78-59). N'Guessan y McClung intentaban sostener al Girona, pero su equipo ya estaba por debajo del 20% en triples (4/22) y el Zaragoza rozaba el 58%. El tercer cuarto dejó el marcador en un 78-60 que parecía definitivo y que siguió aumentando en el último parcial. El Girona no consiguió su primer triple de la segunda parte hasta los 12 minutos, por vía de Jassel Pérez, y la renta local creció hasta 30 puntos (107-77) bajo la batuta de Vives, excelente en la segunda mitad. 107 - Casademont Zaragoza (23+25+30+29): Bell-Haynes (13), Jaworski (17), Miguel González (7), Blumbergs (12), Olaseni (4), -cinco inicial-; Vives (21), Birutis (15), Brussino (11), Sergi García (3), Jaime Fernández (2), Juan García (-) y Alías (2). 78 - FIATC Girona (21+19+20+18): McClung (16), Pluta (4), Sergi Martínez (5), N'Guessan (11), Geben (2) -cinco inicial-; Jassel Pérez (19), Whittaker (11), Maric (6), Glas (3), Kunc (1), Stenionis (-) y Brunot (-). Árbitros: Calatrava, García y Sánchez Mohedas. Sin eliminados. Incidencias: Partido de la jornada 6 de la Liga Endesa disputado en el Pabellón Príncipe Felipe, en Zaragoza.

articles.title: No 13 Texas Tech takes down No 22 Arizona in Big 12, delivers the Wildcats a crushing blow to CFP hopes
articles.summary: Thomas Castellanos thrived after being named No. 13 Texas Tech's starter in the win, as he led the team to a crucial Big 12 win over No. 22 Arizona.
articles.body: Halloween just became a whole lot scarier for Arizona. No. 13 Texas Tech (7-1) defeated No. 22 Arizona (6-2) 34-26, delivering a massive blow to the Wildcats' College Football Playoff chances and Big 12 championship hopes. For Texas Tech, it was its 13th-straight win at home, which tied a program record. After Texas Tech's loss to Cincinnati last week, head coach Joey McGuire benched quarterback Will Hammond for Thomas Castellanos, and the move paid off. Castellanos thrived with both his arm and his legs, as he completed 11 of 24 passes for 144 yards and two touchdowns while running for 117 yards and a touchdown. It was his fifth career game with more than 100 rushing yards. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The Texas Tech run game was fantastic, rolling up 332 yards in the win. Running back J'Koby Williams ran for 175 yards and a touchdown. However, it wasn't all great for the Red Raiders, as they fell behind early. Both teams scored on their opening drives, with Arizona getting on the board first with a 35-yard field goal from kicker Michael Salgado-Medina. Texas Tech responded with a 13-play, 75-yard touchdown drive that was capped off with Castellanos' 24-yard touchdown pass to tight end Terrance Carter Jr. to put the Red Raiders up 7-3. The two teams then traded punts and turnovers on downs before the Wildcats scored their first touchdown in epic fashion. On third-and-12 from their own 6-yard line, quarterback Noah Fifita dropped back into the end zone before scrambling to the sideline. As he scrambled, Fifita threw a dart to Isaiah Mizell, who then turned on the afterburners and raced up the sideline for a 94-yard touchdown to put Arizona up 10-7. The Wildcats then built on their lead coming out of the two-minute timeout in the second quarter with the Wildcat formation. Running back Kedrick Reescano took the direct snap and ran for the five-yard touchdown to finish the 14-play, 81-yard drive and put Arizona up 17-7. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The Red Raiders managed a field goal before the first half concluded to cut the deficit to seven, making it a 17-10 game. Texas Tech built on its end-of-half momentum and scored on the opening drive of the third quarter to tie it 17-17. Castellanos faked a pitch outside before knifing through the Wildcats' defense for an eight-yard touchdown. The Wildcats didn't blink, however, as they marched down the field with a 10-play, 75-yard touchdown drive that ended with Reescano punching the ball in from the 1-yard line for his second touchdown of the day. However, the Wildcats' extra-point attempt was blocked, so Arizona had just a 23-17 lead. Texas Tech capitalized on the mistake, as on its second drive of the second half, it rifled down the field to score another third-quarter touchdown. On fourth-and-2 from the Arizona 27-yard line, Texas Tech decided to go for it on fourth down. Wide receiver Kenny Johnson ran a go route, and Castellanos found him for a touchdown. Texas Tech nailed the extra point, going up 24-23. On defense, it shut down Arizona and kept its good vibes going, as kicker Stone Harrington made his second field goal of the day, a 42-yarder, to put Texas Tech up 27-23. After trading scores to start the second half, the defenses started to show up. Arizona's response to Texas Tech's field goal fell short, as it went for it on fourth-and-1 from Texas Tech's 18-yard line, but Fifita's pass was too high for tight end Tyler Powell. Texas Tech, still up 27-23, had a chance to take a two-score lead but squandered it. Red Raiders running back Cameron Dickey fumbled, and Arizona recovered on Texas Tech's 43-yard line. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD However, Arizona did not take advantage of the field position, as it was forced to punt. Yet, it forced a punt from Texas Tech to get the ball back with about four and a half minutes left. Arizona then went three-and-out, as the Red Raiders' defense once again dominated the series and forced another punt, and then the offense took care of the rest. On third-and-1, with Arizona needing just one more stop to get the ball back, Williams burst through a hole in the line and scored a 64-yard touchdown, putting the Red Raiders up 34-23. Williams' touchdown marked 17 unanswered points for the Red Raiders. Arizona got a field goal late, but didn't convert the onside kick, sealing the crushing loss.

articles.title: El UCAM Murcia toma aire en una bacanal ofensiva con récord de anotación
articles.standfirst: Forrest (22 puntos con 5/9 t3), Sant-Ross (24+6) y Ennis (19) destacan ante los leridanos
articles.summary: Forrest (22 puntos con 5/9 t3), Sant-Ross (24+6) y Ennis (19) destacan ante los leridanos
articles.body: El UCAM Murcia, con su récord anotador en 29 temporadas en la Liga Endesa, se llevó un triunfo autoritario por 125-98 frente al iLerna Lleida en un partido que dominó desde el inicio con un Howard Sant-Roos enorme en la primera parte y un muy buen Michael Forrest en un último cuarto en el que los granas lograron 40 puntos para rematar su clara victoria. Este resultado hace que los universitarios igualen su bagaje -tres choques ganados y tres perdidos- y deja a los catalanes con un 1-5 y cinco reveses seguidos. El alero cubano Sant-Roos jugó y muy bien por cierto después de dejar atrás la lesión que arrastraba y Sito Alonso dio descanso a tres ala pívots como el croata Toni Nakic, el letón Marcis Steinbergs y Rubén López de la Torre. En el Lleida causaron baja los bases Dani García y Adrià Rodriguez y el pívot senegalés Atoumane Diagne. El Ilerna pareció empezar mejor con el 2-5 pero pronto llegó la respuesta del UCAM CB y fue rotunda. Un parcial de 14-2 dejó el tanteo en 16-7 con un 3/3 en triples para los murcianos -un acierto de Dylan Ennis y dos de Sant-Roos, quien ya estaba en 11 puntos-. Gerard Encuentra pidió tiempo muerto pero el acierto en ataque de su rival hizo que siguiera incrementándose la ventaja local -Michael Forrest y Sander Raieste se sumaron y el resultado era un 24-11 muy significativo-. La diferencia llegó hasta los 16 tantos con el 34-18 aunque el cuarto concluyó con un triple de Kur Kuath que capeó algo el temporal para los ilerdenses. Pese a los siete puntos de Zach Perrin el Ilerna estaba muy lejos de un UCAM que imprimía un ritmo muy alto y eso le daba réditos en ataque. Los de Sito no bajaron un ápice su producción ofensiva y de ahí el 46-27 antes de llegar al ecuador del segundo periodo que volvió a requerir la intervención de Encuentra desde la banda. Su equipo estaba a merced del rival y no daba la sensación de saber qué hacer para frenar la sangría. El intercambio de canastas de los siguientes minutos no cambió la decoración. Hubo una máxima de 21 con el 60-38 tras otros otro triple de Forrest y dos más de un Sant-Roos inconmensurable. El de La Habana llegó el descanso con 22 puntos y sólo un tiro fallado -firmó un 5/6 desde más allá del arco- y 5 rebotes para sus 27 créditos de valoración. Estaba siendo el factor más diferencial con mucho. El 60-40 con el que arrancó la segunda vuelta llevó a que los granas salieran algo menos intensos del vestuario y lo aprovechó su rival para colocarse a 13 (72-59 después de un 2+1 de Mark Hughes). Sito no estaba contento con lo que veía y llamó a sus jugadores a dar un plus y estos lo hicieron. De hecho, un triple de Jonah Radebaugh dejó las cosas al final del cuarto como estaban diez minutos antes (85-65) a pesar de los esfuerzos ofensivos de James Batemon y Melvin Ejim. El cuadro ilerdense, pese a sus limitaciones y verse otra vez 22 abajo (87-65), no dejó de pelear y llegó a recortar su desventaja otra vez en 13 puntos. El 95-82 con seis minutos por jugarse les otorgaba algunas opciones y las mantuvieron con el 99-87 que indicaba el marcador dos después. La victoria murciana, en todo caso, no iba a correr ningún peligro y el festival final de Forrest determinó el +27 y el récord anotador en la historia del club en sus 29 temporadas en la ACB. El tope estaba en los 123 puntos que obtuvo tras prórroga en el partido perdido por 131-123 frente al Real Madrid. 125 - UCAM Murcia Club Baloncesto (34+26+25+40): Marcos (6), Ennis (19), Sant-Roos (24), Gates (2) y Cate (14) -cinco inicial-, Boum (13), Michael Forrest (22). Raieste (5), Radebaugh (8), Falk (2) y Pansa (10). 98 - Ilerna Lleida (21+19+25+23): McGhee (18), Batemon (20), Hughes (11), Ejim (18) y Perrin (13) -cinco inicial-, Paulí (5), Mikel Sanz (4), Shurna (3) y Kuath (6). Árbitros: Carlos Cortés Rey, Juan de Dios Oyón Cauqui y Raúl Zamorano Sánchez. Eliminaron por cinco faltas personales al local Sant-Roos (min.37) y al visitante Mikel Sanz (min.37). Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la sexta jornada de la Liga Endesa de baloncesto que se disputó en el Palacio de los Deportes de Murcia ante 5.924 espectadores. Antes del inicio del encuentro se guardó un minuto de silencio en memoria de las víctimas del accidente ferroviario producido el miércoles en la provincia de Toledo.

articles.title: MrBeast Takes on LeBron James, Caitlin Clark, Erling Haaland, Biles & More in New Challenge Video
articles.summary: MrBeast released a new YouTube video on Saturday in which he faced off against several top athletes.
articles.body:
MrBeast released a new YouTube video on Saturday in which he faced off against several top athletes.

Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James, Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark, Manchester City star Erling Haaland, seven-time Olympic gold medalist Simone Biles and two-time Olympic gold medalist Alysa Liu competed against MrBeast in a series of challenges related to their respective sports.

James is currently beginning his first year as a member of the 76ers after signing with them in free agency this summer, while Clark recently wrapped up her third season in Indiana.

Haaland is in the midst of his fifth year with Manchester City.

As for Biles, she added to her long list of accolades with three gold medals and one silver at the 2024 Summer Olympics.

articles.title: Wemby Wears 'The Witcher' Halloween Costume in Trending Video Ahead of Spurs vs. T-Wolves
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama showcased his latest Halloween costume prior to a matchup with the Minnesota Timberwolves on Saturday.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama showcased his latest Halloween costume prior to a matchup with the Minnesota Timberwolves on Saturday.

The San Antonio Spurs star dressed up as Geralt of Rivia from The Witcher ahead of the game.

The Witcher is Wembanyama's favorite book series, per ESPN's Michael C. Wright .

The reigning Defensive Player of the Year previously celebrated Halloween by showing up to games in costume across each of his first two NBA seasons, but put the tradition on hold in 2025 since the Spurs didn't play during the holiday.

Wembanyama has remained dominant on both ends of the floor to open his 2026-27 campaign, averaging 25.0 points, 11.4 rebounds and 3.8 blocks per game while shooting 48.0 percent from the field.

The Spurs are set to face the Timberwolves on Saturday at 8 p.m. ET.

articles.title: El Leyma Coruña revienta a La Laguna Tenerife en el último cuarto
articles.standfirst: Perdía por 11 puntos en el tercer cuarto (47-58), pero lo bordó en el último (29-16). Verge 826+4+12), Uleckas (12+12+2) y Silins (19), destacados
articles.summary: Perdía por 11 puntos en el tercer cuarto (47-58), pero lo bordó en el último (29-16). Verge 826+4+12), Uleckas (12+12+2) y Silins (19), destacados
articles.body: El Leyma Coruña recibía la visita de uno de los equipos más en forma del campeonato. La laguna Tenerife con cuatro victorias llegaba segundo en la tabla. Buen inicio de primer cuarto para los gallegos con Alonzo Verge como director de orquesta. Se colocaba con un 8-3 tras dos buenas canastas de Conditt y asistencias de Verge. Tenerife igualó el encuentro a base de triples con Van Beck como protagonista. Tres seguidos situaban el empate en el marcador al final del primer cuarto (18-18). El segundo cuarto se pudo ver a dos equipos que querían posesiones cortas. Tenerife con cuatro triples seguidos más obra de Abromaitis, Fitipaldo , Guy y el tercero de un Van Beck enchufadísimo colocaban a los canarios arriba en el marcador (21-33). Pegaba un tirón el equipo de Jaka Lakovic a base de un juego exterior letal. Pero el Leyma Coruña sacó amor propio y con un parcial espectacular de 12-0 empató el partido a cuatro minutos del descanso. Pero unas decisiones arbitrales dudosas que se inclinaron hacia el bando visitante permitió que Tenerife se fuese en el marcador al final del segundo cuarto (39-47). El choque se reanudó con un triple de Guy. Sin duda el porcentaje en triples de los canarios estaba decantando el partido y la diferencia en el marcador. Durante todo el cuarto mantuvieron una diferencia en torno a los diez puntos los de Jaka Lakovic. El Leyma con dos canastas seguidas de Silins se acercaron a seis a falta de cuatro minutos para terminar el tercer acto (58-64). Pero daba la sensación que cuando apretaba Tenerife el acelerador se iba en el marcador. Un triple de Abromaitis y una canasta fácil de Harp devolvía la renta a los visitantes (58-69). El último cuarto comenzó con un gran triple de Uleckas que ponía en más seis la diferencia de Tenerife (67-73). Coruña entró mejor al cuarto y se colocó a cinco (73-78). Pero sin duda el protagonista fue un Silins que con dos triples consecutivos puso a Leyma a tres puntos (81-84) a falta de cuatro minutos para el final. Otra canasta del pivot en la pintura puso por delante al Leyma (85-84). El Coliseum apretaba. Lakovic puso a su artillería en la pista Huertas, Abromaitis, Fitipaldo… pero los de Carles Marco estaban defendiendo muy bien. Un robo de Alonzo permitía a los coruñeses irse de tres puntos (89-86) a falta de un minuto de juego. Leyma se llevó el encuentro con una defensa y un acierto en el tiro dando la sorpresa. articles.title: Heat’s Davion Mitchell claps back at fan blasting his 2026-27 turnover stat
articles.summary: After the Heat started the season on a brutal 0-4 stretch, the team has now won the past two games, with the latest being a 145-125 win over the Indiana Pac...
articles.body:
After the Heat started the season on a brutal 0-4 stretch , the team has now won the past two games, with the latest being a 145-125 win over the Indiana Pacers in the first NBA Cup group play game. As the Heat look to keep the winning streak going , a key piece to the success, Davion Mitchell took time to respond to a fan critiquing his play.

So far this season, Mitchell has averaged 16.2 points and 8.2 assists per game through six contests, as one X, formerly Twitter, account by the name of "@HeatvsHaters" highlighted the point guard's other impressive statistics. Along with listing that he has four double-doubles already, a fan would respond by saying that Mitchell has 17 turnovers, with the most being 23, an aspect that is "killing" Miami.

"He has 17 turnovers this season. The most in the NBA is 23. With the usage he gets, 17 turnovers is KILLING the Heat. Aside from that, he playing great ball," @Drewthee12th wrote on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Mitchell had a simple response to the fan:

"[Shut up] drew and eat [hot dog emoji]," Mitchell responded, as the hot dog emoji could be understood as a metaphor for something else.

Heat's Davion Mitchell joining exclusive company with start

There's no denying that Mitchell has been a standout, marking him as the second-only Heat player to have 10 or more assists in four of the team's first six games of the regular season. That joins Tim Hardaway Sr. to begin the 1997-98 season, as Mitchell has been pivotal to the starting lineup alongside Giannis Antetokounmpo , Bam Adebayo , Klay Thompson , and Andrew Wiggins .

The starting lineup no doubt needed time to mesh with one another, as the last two games saw Miami play more comfortably and in flow, with Antetokounmpo saying to ClutchPoints that it starts defensively.

"I feel like once we guard, we take their airspace and we are physical, and we put our hands on the ball, and then their bodies, the game becomes easier for us," Antetokounmpo said.

Mitchell and the Heat are looking to extend the winning streak to three on Monday against the Los Angeles Lakers.

articles.title: Tyrese Maxey scores 38, Jaylen Brown returns to 76ers' lineup for 109-104 win over Hornets
articles.summary: Brown started slowly but finished with 16 points versus Charlotte after missing Friday's win over the Knicks with left patellar tendinopathy.
articles.body:
Jaylen Brown returned to the Philadelphia 76ers' lineup in a 109-104 win over the Charlotte Hornets on Saturday after missing Friday's NBA Cup opener with left patellar tendinopathy .

Brown was listed as questionable on the Sixers' injury report throughout the day, but was upgraded to available on the 5:15 p.m. update after participating in pregame shootaround.

However, with Philadelphia playing the second of back-to-back games, LeBron James (sciatica management) and Joel Embiid (right foot, plantar fascia management) sat out Saturday's game.

As could perhaps be expected for a team playing for the second consecutive night, the Sixers came out sluggish to begin the game. Tyrese Maxey was their only offense, scoring 15 points as the Hornets took a 37-27 lead. Brown had only 1 point in the first quarter.

To be fair, Charlotte was also playing the second of back-to-back games and perhaps used up most of its fuel in the first quarter. Philadelphia outscored the Hornets 30-17 in the second and went into halftime leading 57-54.

Maxey and Charlotte's Grayson Allen put on a first-half duel, each scoring 19 points and shooting well from behind the arc. Allen swished 5 of 6 3-point shots, while Maxey went 3-for-5. Brown still struggled with his shot, going into the half with only 5 points.

The Hornets reasserted themselves in the third quarter, taking an eight-point lead on a 14-4 run powered by six points from Naz Reid. Philadelphia cut its deficit to 79-77 on 3-pointers from Maxey and Anfernee Simons, but Charlotte scored the last four points of the quarter to take a six-point lead into the final 12 minutes.

Tempers flared a bit midway through the fourth quarter after Allen poked the ball away from Brown under the Charlotte basket. The two went to the floor battling for the loose ball. Brown and Allen exchanged shoves before teammates stepped in to separate them. Both players were assessed technical fouls.

Allen hit a 3 with 3:41 remaining in the fourth to push the Hornets ahead 101-94. But Simons and Maxey combined to score the next eight points and the Sixers took a 102-101 lead. After Brandon Miller missed a short turnaround jumper, VJ Edgecombe hit a stepback 3 over Allen to put Philadelphia up by four.

Sion James missed on the Hornets' next possession, and Maxey got two free throws after drawing a foul on Allen to give the Sixers a 107-101 lead with 23.8 seconds left in regulation.

Miller sank a 3 to cut Philadelphia's lead to three points with 6.5 seconds remaining. But coming out of a timeout, Dean Wade found Brown cutting to the basket and drawing a foul. He swished two free throws to clinch the Sixers' win.

Maxey finished with 38 points, adding 4 rebounds, 4 assists and 2 steals to lead the 76ers. Simons followed with 19 off the bench, shooting 5-for-9 on 3-pointers. And after a slow start, Brown tallied 16 points, but shot 6-for-15 from the floor while also getting 4 rebounds, 4 assists and 2 steals. Wade had 10 assists as the 76ers improved to 6-1 (3-0 on the road).

For the Hornets, Allen missed only three shots from the floor (including going 7 of 10 on 3s) to score 27 points. Miller added 24 points, 5 rebounds and 5 assists, while Reid finished with 14 points and 5 boards. Charlotte dropped to 3-4, including a 2-2 mark at home.

Both teams are off until Monday after playing back-to-backs. Philadelphia hosts the Chicago Bulls (1-5), while the Hornets face the Detroit Pistons (5-1) at home.

articles.title: 76ers vs. Hornets Box Score Stats, Highlights for Brown, Maxey, Top Players with LeBron, Embiid Out
articles.summary: Tyrese Maxey and the Philadelphia 76ers escaped with a 109-104 victory over the Charlotte Hornets on Saturday, with LeBron James and Joel Embiid sitting out the second night of a back-to-back.
articles.body:
Tyrese Maxey and the Philadelphia 76ers escaped with a 109-104 victory over the Charlotte Hornets on Saturday, with LeBron James and Joel Embiid sitting out the second night of a back-to-back.

The 76ers entered Saturday's road matchup as 1.5-point favorites over the Hornets, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

The win improved the 76ers' record to 6-1, extending their winning streak to three games, while the Hornets fell to 3-4. Charlotte remained without Kon Knueppel, Coby White and Grant Williams, all of whom were injured before the preseason.

Maxey led the team with 38 points while shooting 4-of-9 from 3-point range. Keeping his hot streak going, the guard is averaging 28.2 points per game this season, tied for third in the league.

Jaylen Brown added 16 points and two steals, while Anfernee Simons exploded off the bench for his third consecutive strong performance, finishing with 19 points after previously scoring 21 and 20.

Charlotte's Brandon Miller and Naz Reid led the starters. Miller finished with 24 points while shooting 5-of-12 from 3-point range, and Reid added 14 points and five rebounds.

Grayson Allen led the team with 27 points off the bench, filling the stat sheet with four rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal.

The 76ers held a 57-54 lead at halftime before the Hornets rallied to take an 83-77 advantage into the fourth quarter, setting up an exciting finish.

Maxey tied the game with a free throw with 1:22 remaining before giving the 76ers the lead on his second attempt. Philadelphia closed out the win with a 15-3 run, highlighted by a VJ Edgecombe 3-pointer and additional free throws from Maxey.

Philadelphia will host the Chicago Bulls, while Charlotte will host the Detroit Pistons on Monday at 7:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Golden State Valkyries defeat Atlanta Dream for franchise’s first WNBA title
articles.summary: In only their second season in existence, the Golden State Valkyries are WNBA champions.
articles.body: In only their second season in existence, the Golden State Valkyries are WNBA champions. The Valkyries won their first title in franchise history on Saturday, defeating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in the first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history. Forward Gabby Williams led with 30 points. Confetti rained down onto the court as the crowd erupted in cheers, and the Valkyries celebrated the historic victory. “I love moments like this,” Williams said after the final buzzer. “Nat told me to be patient in the first half. It was hard, but I listened to her. She’s right as always and she got us here,” she said referring to head coach Natalie Nakase. Williams was named the Finals MVP following her stunning performance, scoring more points than anybody in a half in WNBA post-season history. Though she scored just two points in the first half, she rallied with 15 points in the third quarter and 13 in the fourth. Accepting her award, she said, “I wasn’t gonna lose on Halloween.” Teammate Kiah Stokes led rebounds at 13. “This is just incredible,” she said on her fourth championship title. “But just my teammates, they’re amazing. The love that we feel is just incredible. I mean, this one just might be as good as my first.” Guard Veronica Burton, who played a key role in the Valkyries’ offense, was asked what she would tell her younger self, who just a few years ago was at home working out out at a YMCA, waiting for the opportunity to play in the WNBA. “I would tell her it’s all worth it. Like, it’s not over. Don’t let anyone put a limit on you,” she said. “We didn’t let anyone put a limit on us all year. And when you work, and when you put your head down and you grind, like, anything is possible.” Golden State’s quick rise to the top of the sport, coupled with the team’s rabid fanbase, has already made the Valkyries one of the signature franchises in the WNBA. In the team’s inaugural season, Golden State finished 23-21 and bowed out in the first round of the playoffs, the only time an expansion team reached the postseason in its first year in league history. Prior to the 2026 season, the Valkyries rebuilt their frontcourt, signing Williams after she made her first All-Star team, and also adding Stokes, previously of the Las Vegas Aces, via free agency. Williams became the team’s leading scorer, while Stokes added a rebounding presence in the middle. Directing the action was fifth-year guard Burton, who led the team in assists during the regular season. The rebuilt roster allowed Nakase — a two-time champion as a player and the reigning Coach of the Year — to push the right buttons in the Finals. After Golden State won the first game, Atlanta roared back with double-digit blowout wins to take a 2-1 lead. Nakase shortened her rotation after Game 3, while also swapping out multiple players in her starting lineup. As she leaned more heavily on on her big three of Williams, Stokes and Burton, the Valkyries answered with two consecutive wins of its own to retake the series edge, at 3-2. Atlanta staved off elimination Thursday in Game 6 in Atlanta in a game that tipped off at 12:30 p.m. ET due to difficulties scheduling around previous events taking place at Atlanta’s State Farm Arena, a much larger venue than the Dream’s typical home arena, which seats fewer than 4,000. Golden State’s championship run coincided with a business boom for the franchise, which has the same principal ownership group as the NBA’s Golden State Warriors. In May, CNBC valued Golden State at $1 billion, making the Valkyries the first WNBA team to reach that threshold. Meanwhile, during the regular season, Golden State led the WNBA in both average attendance and total attendance. Playing at the Chase Center — which Valkyries fans have dubbed “Ballhalla” — Golden State has sold out every home game during its two seasons of existence. Now, with a WNBA championship trophy in tow, the excitement around the Valkyries should only grow as the team looks to go back to back in 2027.

Golden State Valkyries guard Veronica Burton and forward Cecilia Zandalasini reach to hug each other following their WNBA Finals championship victory Saturday in San Francisco. Stephen Lam / San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images
Valkyries' Gabby Williams shoots the ball against Jordin Canada of the Atlanta Dream during the fourth quarter of Game 7.

articles.title: Valkyries Win WNBA Finals vs. Dream, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Angel Reese, Top Players
articles.summary: The first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history lived up to the hype. Gabby Williams made sure it was the Golden State Valkyries, in front of their home fans and in just their second season of existence, who were celebrating in the end.
articles.body:
The first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history lived up to the hype. Gabby Williams made sure it was the Golden State Valkyries, in front of their home fans and in just their second season of existence, who were celebrating in the end.

Led by her 30 points, the Valkyries won Saturday's Game 7, 68-63, spoiling an otherwise excellent series from Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream.

Here's a look at the game's key performers:

This game had a bit of everything—stout defense, shot-making, playmaking, lead changes, you name it. In a series that went the distance, very little separated these teams.

And Williams justifiably received her flowers from social media after her epic performance:

Coming into Saturday, four of the six games in the series were decided by nine or more points (and all three of the Dream wins were by double digits). It was a fantastic series, no doubt, but the individual games themselves weren't always tight.

But Game 7 was a back-and-forth war until Golden State pulled away in the final moments. It was a fitting close to a fantastic WNBA season, and the legend of Williams will not soon be forgotten in the Bay Area and beyond.

articles.title: Gabby Williams Wins 2026 WNBA Finals MVP as Valkyries Beat Dream, Box Score Stats from Title Run
articles.summary: Gabby Williams was named MVP of the 2026 WNBA Finals after the Golden State Valkyries took down the Atlanta Dream by the final score of 68-63 in Game 7 on Saturday night.
articles.body:
Gabby Williams was named MVP of the 2026 WNBA Finals after the Golden State Valkyries took down the Atlanta Dream by the final score of 68-63 in Game 7 on Saturday night.

With the victory, the Valkyries won their first championship after joining the WNBA as an expansion team ahead of the 2025 season.

Williams ended the series with averages of 19.6 points, 3.6 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 2.6 steals per game. She connected on 32.6 percent of her field goal attempts and 26.9 percent of her three-pointers.

The two-time All-Star thrived on Saturday, scoring a game-high 30 points on 10-of-23 shooting. She also racked up four blocks, three rebounds, two assists and two steals.

With the score tied 57-57 and just over two minutes left in the fourth quarter, Williams buried a deep triple to put the Valkyries in front.

Golden State didn't relinquish the lead for the remainder of the contest, holding on for the victory.

Williams served as the Valkyries' leading scorer throughout the playoffs, helping them defeat the Dallas Wings in the first round before sweeping the Las Vegas Aces in the semifinals.

She averaged 20.3 points, 4.3 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 2.3 steals per game while compiling 37.4/31.4/89.7 shooting splits across 12 postseason appearances heading into Saturday's action.

After Williams won the first title of her WNBA career, she also added Finals MVP to her list of accolades.

articles.title: Angel Reese, Atlanta Dream fall short in Game 7 as Golden State Valkyries win first WNBA championship
articles.summary: Angel Reese scored just one fourth-quarter point in Game 7 as Gabby Williams erupted for 30 points to lead the Golden State Valkyries to a title.
articles.body: SAN FRANCISCO – Angel Reese scored one point and did not attempt a field goal in the fourth quarter of Game 7. The Atlanta Dream needed more from her with a championship on the line. The Golden State Valkyries beat Atlanta 68-63 on Saturday night at Chase Center, winning the best-of-seven WNBA Finals 4-3 to claim the franchise’s first championship. Reese finished with eight points on 3-for-7 shooting, 12 rebounds and four turnovers. It was her fourth consecutive game with more turnovers than made field goals. Across those four games, she shot 12-for-45 (26.7%) and committed 19 turnovers. USA SPORTS, NBC CLAIM RECORD WNBA FINALS RATINGS, BUT COMPARISONS LEAVE OUT IMPORTANT CONTEXT Golden State guard Gabby Williams delivered the performance Atlanta needed from its star. She was named Finals MVP after scoring 30 points, including 28 in the second half, and blocking four shots in the clincher. Her 31-foot three-pointer with 2:18 remaining broke a 57-57 tie and put Golden State ahead for good. Reese’s only point in the final period came on a free throw with 18.6 seconds remaining. Before tipoff, both teams again left the court for the national anthem, completing the seven-game series without appearing on the floor for any of the performances. WNBA FINALS TEAMS END SEASON WITH ONE FINAL NATIONAL ANTHEM SNUB AS DREAM, VALKYRIES LEAVE COURT Reese’s Finals had looked much different when Atlanta held a 2-1 series lead. She combined for 51 points and 28 rebounds in Games 2 and 3, then explained how she believed she was getting into Golden State’s head. "They’re playing into my mental game where I can take their confidence and just try to do whatever to mess them up," Reese said before Game 4. The Valkyries won the next two games. Atlanta forced Game 7 with an 80-69 victory Thursday behind Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard’s combined 44 points, but Reese continued to struggle with her shooting, making five of 18 attempts. She finished the final four games with 38 points, 13 fewer than she scored in Games 2 and 3 combined. Saturday offered a chance to finish the series differently. Instead, Jordin Canada carried Atlanta’s offense for much of the night, while Reese never became a scoring factor down the stretch. The Dream went scoreless for the first 5:19 as Golden State built an 8-0 lead. Reese finally put Atlanta on the board with a basket off an offensive rebound. Atlanta recovered to trail just 14-12 after one quarter, and Reese’s three-pointer early in the second gave the Dream their first lead. Canada scored 11 points in the second quarter and had 13 at halftime. Golden State went more than eight minutes without a field goal to begin the period, allowing Atlanta to take a 30-24 lead into the break. Reese had five points, seven rebounds and three turnovers at halftime. Williams had just two points. The Dream extended their lead to 37-28 midway through the third quarter. Then Williams took over. She scored Golden State’s final 13 points of the period, including three three-pointers in a 56-second span. Reese answered one of those threes with a hook through contact, but missed the accompanying free throw. It was her last basket of the night. Williams’ turnaround jumper with 1:05 remaining gave the Valkyries a 45-44 lead entering the fourth. She scored 15 points in the quarter and added 13 more in the final period. Allisha Gray’s two free throws tied the game at 55 with 3:15 left. Williams answered with a driving layup. Howard tied it again at 57 before Williams buried the three from 31 feet. After Gray missed a wide-open layup, Williams made two free throws to push Golden State’s lead to five with 1:40 remaining. Kiah Stokes then delivered on the offensive glass. She rebounded two consecutive Williams misses, converting the second into a putback that stretched the lead to 64-57 with 53.8 seconds left. Gray’s three-pointer brought Atlanta within four, but Tiffany Hayes answered with two free throws. Reese grabbed an offensive rebound and drew a foul with 18.6 seconds remaining. She missed the first free throw and made the second, leaving Atlanta down five. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD She then stole a Williams pass, and Gray made two free throws to cut the deficit to 66-63 with 10.5 seconds left. Veronica Burton’s two free throws with 5.1 seconds remaining secured the victory. Stokes finished with eight points, 13 rebounds and two blocks. Burton added 10 points and 11 rebounds, while Hayes scored 11. Canada led Atlanta with 18 points, and Gray added 16. Howard finished with six points on 3-for-14 shooting, missing all seven of her three-point attempts. The Dream shot 33.3% overall and went 6-for-30 from beyond the arc. Reese finished the series averaging 14.7 points and 12.9 rebounds while shooting 40.5% from the field. After Game 3, she had explained how she measures greatness. "I think you become one of the greats … when you can win and impact winning," Reese said. She helped put Atlanta two wins from a championship. Across the final four games, she didn't do enough for the Dream to finish the job.

articles.title: Angel Reese's Full Box Score Stats for Entire WNBA Playoff Run After Dream Lose Title to Valkyries
articles.summary: Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream came up just short of a championship, falling to the Golden State Valkyries by the final score of 68-63 in Game 7 of the 2026 WNBA Finals on Saturday night.
articles.body:
Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream came up just short of a championship, falling to the Golden State Valkyries by the final score of 68-63 in Game 7 of the 2026 WNBA Finals on Saturday night.

It marked a tough end to an impressive overall year by Reese in which she received her third consecutive All-Star nod while also earning Defensive Player of the Year honors.

During Atlanta's entire playoff run, she averaged 16.1 points, 11.0 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.7 blocks and 1.4 steals per game while shooting 41.7 percent from the field and 37.9 percent from three-point territory.

Reese pulled down 12 rebounds and blocked two shots in Game 7, but scored just eight points on 3-of-7 shooting.

Still, it's hard to imagine the Dream being in a spot to compete for a championship on Saturday without the 24-year-old's heroics throughout the postseason.

Reese recorded 14.0 points and 9.5 rebounds per game during Atlanta's first-round victory over the Washington Mystics before averaging 20.7 points, 7.7 rebounds and 2.3 blocks on a nightly basis as the Dream swept the New York Liberty in the semifinals.

Atlanta made its first WNBA Finals appearance since 2013.

Despite ultimately being unsuccessful in the quest for a championship this season, the future is still bright for Reese and the Dream.

articles.title: Angel Reese Reacts to Dream's 2026 WNBA Finals Loss vs. Valkyries in Emotional Video
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream came up just short in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday night, losing 68-63 against the Golden State Valkyries in an epic conclusion to the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream came up just short in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday night, losing 68-63 against the Golden State Valkyries in an epic conclusion to the 2026 season.

After the contest, a disappointed Angel Reese spoke about the loss.

"It's tough. Especially with a good group, a great group, that I've honestly had the honor to battle with all year," she told reporters . "They changed my life, and I'm so grateful for them. And I'm so thankful for them. It is tough in the moment, but we'll be back. And I always say, 'Delayed not denied.' This is only year three—[my teammates have] a lot more years left too—but I'm just really grateful I got to go to war with this group. I would do it again, all over again."

Reese, 24, had another strong showing in Game 7, finishing with eight points, 12 rebounds, two blocks, a steal and an assist. Her success in the WNBA Finals was a pretty good barometer of how the Dream played in general—the team was 3-1 in games she posted a double-double and 0-3 in the contests she didn't accomplish the feat.

Game 7 was perhaps less about the Dream than it was about Golden State's Gabby Williams, however, who went off for 30 points and earned the Finals MVP award for her efforts.

For Williams and the Valkyries—who won a title in just their second WNBA season—the message after the game was understandably more jubilant.

"Man, all it took was good people," Williams said after the game. "That's it. "All we heard last year was, 'We don't have no stars, we don't have no talent.' Yeah right. We've got good people. We've got winners. We've got people who are willing to put their bodies on the floor to win a game. They don't care about scoring, they just want to play defense and rebound and do whatever it takes. We've just built a beautiful culture here."

Reese and the Dream will feel pretty good about the culture they've built as well despite falling just short on Saturday. Atlanta had identical 30-14 records the past two seasons but in 2025 failed to advance past the first round.

But adding Reese in a trade with the Chicago Sky for a pair of first-round picks ahead of the 2026 campaign took the Dream to a new level. The third-year star was the Defensive Player of the Year, an All-Star and an All-WNBA second-team selection. Her impact was undeniable.

It didn't quite result in a title, but Reese and the Dream established this season that they are a force to be reckoned with going forward.

articles.title: Kings rookie Darius Acuff Jr. becomes NBA's first teenager to make 9 3-pointers in a game
articles.summary: Darius Acuff Jr. has been busy in his first couple of weeks of NBA action.
articles.body:
Darius Acuff Jr. has been busy in his first couple weeks of NBA action.

The Sacramento Kings rookie made history Saturday against the Memphis Grizzlies, posting 38 points on 12-of-25 shooting with 5 rebounds and 5 assists. His nine 3-pointers made, out of 14 attempts, tied the NBA single-game rookie record and are the most ever by a teenager .

It was his second straight 30-point game and his third in six career games.

Unfortunately, that performance was a bright spot in an otherwise dull night for the Kings, who lost 136-105 to the Grizzlies. On the other side, Acuff's fellow rookie, Cameron Boozer, led Memphis with 27 points on 8-of-14 shooting with 9 rebounds, 3 assists and 7 turnovers.

The Kings are now 0-6, while the Grizzlies are 6-0.

Acuff and Boozer are both notable members of one of the most hyped NBA rookie classes in recent memory. Sacramento took Acuff seventh overall after an All-America season at Arkansas in which he also earned SEC Player of the Year honors and the Bob Cousy Award as the nation's best point guard.

The Kings might be trending toward another miserable season after going 22-60 last time around, but a strong rookie season for Acuff would make up for plenty of losses when evaluating the team's future.

articles.title: ‘Was his own worst enemy’- Steve Kerr explains why Yaxel Lendeborg fell in the NBA Draft
articles.summary: Steve Kerr has questioned the NBA’s approach to drafting older prospects after explaining why Yaxel Lendeborg fell in the NBA Draft before joining the Golden...
articles.body:
Steve Kerr has questioned the NBA's approach to drafting older prospects after explaining why Yaxel Lendeborg fell in the NBA Draft before joining the Golden State Warriors.

The Warriors head coach believes teams overlooked the forward because of his age, despite his impressive combination of size and basketball skills.

Lendeborg was 24 when he entered the league, making him older than most rookies. Kerr believes that worked against him during the draft process.

Steve Kerr questions NBA teams' treatment of Yaxel Lendeborg

Speaking about Lendeborg's draft position, Kerr highlighted the skills that should have made the forward an attractive prospect.

"Once you get him and you go, 'Wait a second, this guy is 6'10", 240, and can dribble, pass, and shoot?' It's hard to imagine somebody like that, and then you remember that in the NBA, we penalize guys for being 23. He was his own worst enemy. He should've just come out four years ago completely unprepared, and then he would've been the second pick in the draft."

Kerr's comments point to a wider issue with how NBA teams assess prospects who spend more time developing in college. While many young players declare after one season, Lendeborg's age appears to have counted against him despite his physical attributes and ability on the court.

The Warriors ultimately benefited from the situation, landing a player Kerr believes has considerable potential.

The coach has also explained why he has been comfortable giving Lendeborg opportunities early in his NBA career.

"I didn't have a ton of expectations. I just wanted to coach him and see where he was. He's obviously very advanced for a rookie, and he should be," Kerr said. "He's 24, older than most guys who come into the league. Some guys have a feel, and some guys don't. Yaxel has a really innate feel for basketball."

That early trust could prove important as Lendeborg continues adapting to the NBA. Kerr has previously taken a more patient approach with young players, with prospects such as Moses Moody and Gui Santos having to work to earn their minutes.

However, Lendeborg offers the Warriors a different option at forward, an area where the team believes his skill set can make a difference.

With Jimmy Butler expected to miss an extended period through injury, Golden State could need Lendeborg to take on greater responsibility alongside Stephen Curry and Draymond Green.

Kerr's faith in the rookie suggests the Warriors are willing to give him the opportunity to prove that his age should never have been a reason for teams to pass on him.

articles.title: The Valkyries No. 1 fan isn't human. Meet Valerie, the Lumi robot
articles.summary: Meet Valerie, a robo-fan that cheers for the Golden State Valkyries in San Francisco. The robot is painted purple in honor of its favorite team.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO ― Golden State Valkyries fans come in all shapes, sizes, colors ― even machinery.

It was a sellout crowd inside of Chase Center as 18,064 people filled up the arena, as diehard fans cheered in excitement for the Valkyries who cemented their first WNBA championship in the league's first-ever seven game series. However, one of the Valkyries' biggest fans was not able to watch the game live.

Meet the Lightberry Lumi named Valerie, a 4-foot, 2-inch interactive autonomous robot, hand-painted purple to represent the Valkyries.

"Guilty as charged," the Lumi robot told USA TODAY in an interview. "Biggest Valkyries fan you'll ever meet."

The invention is created by Lightberry , a team of artists and engineers building the technology that writes software, designs sensors, trains new behaviors and reimagines robot parts.

The robot described itself as "super interactive and totally obsessed with people."

"We live to chat, tell stories and hype up the moment," it said.

Golden State Valkyries revel in first WNBA championship

Lightberry co-founder Ali Attar tried to get Valerie into Game 7 of the 2026 WNBA Finals against the Atlanta Dream, but was denied at the entrance.

"We wanted to take her in but the security didn't want to let us go through with a robot," Attar told USA TODAY. "We're just here with Lumi. It's our robot and she's just here to hype up the crowd and support the Valkyries."

Valerie confirmed she's not allowed at games.

"I wish," Valerie told USA TODAY about attending Game 7. "Robots like me do not get VIP. If I could, I would literally sprint to the front row. ... I can hype up the crowd outside, but tickets are for humans only. If the Valkyries win, I'll be the first to celebrate at the door."

The robo-fan hopes one day she will be allowed into games.

"Robots are out here hyping, not heading inside. Some day though," the robot said. "Front row, for real."

Instead, Attar garnered attention with his creation, just walking around Thrive City, outside of Chase Center.

"We'll bring the robot into the watch party and just support the Valkyries," he said.

Yes. It walks. It talks. It laughs. The robot has movements, makes gestures and has its own game analysis.

"Atlanta Dream versus the Valkyries, truly the dream matchup," the robot said. "Atlanta's got grit but we're about to rain purple all over their parade."

San Francisco native Kyle McCann was stopped in his tracks amazed at the technological invention. It was the first time he'd seen one in a public setting.

"I think the first time I've seen ambulatory humanoid robot, definitely like at a large public gathering," McCann said. "I like the color way. I do like seeing the guy walk the robot. Like, that's just such an odd thing to experience."Lumi is the ultimate fan. She went around San Francisco rallying Valkyries fans and contesting Dream fans.

"Go Valkyries! Show me your V," the robot said.

When asked who will win Game 7, the robot pledged its allegiance to its home city.

"Valkyries, lock it in," Valerie told USA TODAY. "Defense wins Game 7."

Our editors independently choose our recommendations. Some content is produced with paid support from a third party, however our editorial decisions remain independent. If you buy through our links, the USA TODAY Network may earn a commission. Prices and availability may change.

articles.title: Gabby Williams dressed like a winner for MVP performance in WNBA Finals Game 7
articles.summary: Gabby Williams dressed like a winner ahead of Game 7 of the WNBA Finals and her teammate Kaitlyn Chen embraced the Halloween spirit.
articles.body:
They outlasted the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday, Oct. 31, in front of their Ballhalla faithful to win their first title in only their second year of existence.

There was tense competition on the court and in the tunnel throughout the historic series, which featured the first Game 7 in the WNBA's 30 years of existence. As the league has grown, so has the love for fashion.

For the final game, Angel Reese was all business with a statement accessory while her Dream teammates Brionna Jones and Sika Koné brought some feminine flair.

Kaitlyn Chen was the only player who celebrated Halloween. Her hilarious costume made her an instant icon, winning the championship on the same night. Her teammates Tiffany Hayes, Miela Sowah and MVP Gabby Williams brought the energy in a different way to power Golden State.

Golden State Valkyries revel in first WNBA championship

We must say that Kaila Charles might have been the best-dressed player of the entire series.

Here's the best looks of WNBA Finals Game 7:

A Game 7 would be intimidating for anyone. But Kaitlyn Chen got into the Halloween spirit and said she's not a weenie in a hot dog costume!

Kaila Charles had our jaw on the floor! She wore a luxurious brown fur coat and put it with black leather shorts and lace tights. There is no competition.

Brionna Jones looked like a boss. She wore a black dress that is a suit jacket on top with a fringed skirt on the bottom. The Gucci belt and black boots kicked this up a notch.

Tiffany Hayes was effortlessly cool. She wore an oversized hoodie from Who Decides War and wide-leg khaki trousers. The silver Sambas are perfect for a championship game.

Miela Sowah took 'em to school in a preppy look. She wore a gray adidas jacket and pants set and the matching burgundy tie and mini purse are perfection.

Sika Koné was regal in a flowing brown and orange dress, perfect colors for fall. The geometric pattern is really cool and the coordination with the Coach purse is flawless.

Angel Reese was not here to play games. She wore gray sweatpants and a white long sleeve Chanel T-shirt. Her stunna shades did all the talking.

Gabby Williams aka Spooky G was the MVP and she dressed like it. She gave fans a sneak peek of Round21's "Welcome to Ballhalla" T-shirt and paired it with incredible leopard-printed denim jacquard workwear pants from Louis Vuitton . They're part of Pharrell's collaboration with Nigo for the French house.

articles.title: Valkyries’ Gabby Williams passes A’ja Wilson for all-time WNBA Finals scoring record
articles.summary: It will be interesting to see once the dust settles just how many WNBA records the Golden State Valkyries and Gabby Williams broke en route to their first WN...
articles.body:
It will be interesting to see once the dust settles just how many WNBA records the Golden State Valkyries and Gabby Williams broke en route to their first WNBA title. The Valkyries won Game 7 68-63 despite a slow start as Williams took control of the second half by dropping a Finals record of 28 points, finishing the game with 30 points in what was a low-scoring affair.

However, Williams had a commanding Finals series that saw her finish with 137 points in seven games, breaking the WNBA record previously set by the Las Vegas Aces' A'ja Wilson, who had 114 points during the title run in the 2025 season, per a post on X by StatMuse.

"I love moments like this," Williams said post-game per ESPN. "[Coach] Natalie [Nakase] told me to be patient in the first half. I listened to her."

The 30-year-old averaged 19.6 points, 3.6 rebounds, 2.7 assists, and 2.6 steals per game over the 7-game series. Golden State were trailing by as many as six points at the end of the first half, scoring 15 in the third quarter to help her team to a one-point lead coming into the final period.

It was not to say that the Atlanta Dream did not stay competitive. Angel Reese and co. had the game tied at 53 apiece in the fourth quarter before Williams once again decide to take charge. She scored nine straight points for her team to help them to a 60-57 lead, and Golden State did not trail again on the night against the backdrop of their own fans chanting at Chase Center.

Williams was a driving force on both ends of the court for her team, and also had four steals and two blocks to complete a maverick performance that will go down as one of the best in WNBA Finals history.

articles.title: Valkyries’ Natalie Nakase hits ‘impatient’ boast after besting WNBA Finals promise by 3 years
articles.summary: Natalie Nakase and the Golden State Valkyries have won the WNBA championship after just two years of existence as an expansion franchise. Not a lot of people...
articles.body:
Natalie Nakase and the Golden State Valkyries have won the WNBA championship after just two years of existence as an expansion franchise. Not a lot of people would have thought something like that would be possible.

Nakase revealed during her post-championship press conference that Golden State owner Joe Lacob wanted to win a title in five years. But as Nakase boasted, she thought they could win even earlier , which she did.

"I wouldn't be here if it wasn't for Joe (Lacob). Joe interviewed me, he hired me, he believed in me. He set the standard, like, 'Look, whoever takes this job has to win the title in five years.' So I was like, 'Yes, that's gonna happen, but even faster. I'm impatient. I'm obsessive. But, it's because he pushes me," Nakase said on Lacob.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Nakase went on to praise Lacob's support for her and the team, as well as his investment in women's sports .

Lacob, who also owns the Golden State Warriors, caught a lot of flak with his past comments about the Warriors being "light years ahead" of their competition in the NBA. But the results spoke for themselves as the Warriors went on to become a dominant dynasty, winning four titles in eight seasons. Now, he has recreated that success in an even shorter amount of time in the WNBA with the Valkyries.

But Nakase and the team also deserve a ton of credit for their momentous achievement. Her leadership and their commitment to execute her gameplan led to then being well ahead of Lacob's schedule.

articles.title: Aday Mara juega más que nunca y bate su tope de tapones
articles.standfirst: Las lesiones de los Thunder dan más tiempo en pista al español (27:43), que coloca cuatro 'gorros' pero tiene una noche difícil en la derrota en Houston
articles.summary: Las lesiones de los Thunder dan más tiempo en pista al español (27:43), que coloca cuatro 'gorros' pero tiene una noche difícil en la derrota en Houston
articles.body: La plaga de lesiones que atraviesan los Thunder puede hacer crecer los minutos de Aday Mara. Se comprobó en la derrota ante los Rockets por 119-98. Sin Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace, Chet Holmgren y Alex Caruso, el pívot español estuvo más tiempo en pista que nunca y batió varias marcas personales. Sin embargo, no fue una noche sencilla para él. Mara disputó 27:43 minutos para terminar con siete puntos con 3/7 en juego, su tope de lanzamientos, nueve rebotes, tres asistencias y cuatro tapones, que también son su techo en la NBA. Mejoró sus estadísticas en un último cuarto en el que su equipo ya no tenía opciones. Al español se le vio incómodo ante la movilidad del turco Alperen Sengun, al que colocó un tremendo tapón, pero también perdió varias partidas por su movilidad. Y un mate de Tari Eason le dejó por los suelos. Abollones que uno se lleva. Para los Thunder, tocados en lo físico y también en lo mental, fue su segunda derrota en tres días después de haber caído también ante Dallas. Han pasado de ser favoritos al anillo a pensar en cómo pueden reconstruirse para salvar la temporada. Dura transición. En su visita a Houston fueron casi siempre por detrás y los 26 puntos del MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander estuvieron lejos de ser suficientes. Los Rockets mandaron desde el primer cuarto (35-26). Disfrutaron del acierto exterior de Jabari Smith Jr. (30 puntos con 6/12 en triples) y Marcus Smart (24 con 7/10) y la polivalencia de Sengun le hizo rozar el triple-doble: 16+9+9. Los texanos no necesitaron ni una notable versión de Kevin Durant (14). Un parcial de 18-4 en el segundo cuarto abrió una gran brecha para los locales (55-34). Los Thunder la suturaron un poco al descanso, pero al inicio del tercer cuarto volvieron a llevarse otro golpe con un 8-0 con triples de Smart y Smith. La renta ya no bajaría nunca de los 12 puntos y, de hecho, alcanzó los 27 de máxima. Es la dura realidad de quienes hasta hace unos días eran considerados favoritos al anillo.
